title: NY State Assembly · District 24
area: Central Queens, including Hollis, Jamaica Hills, Queens Village, Glen Oaks and parts of Richmond Hill and Jamaica.

context.text: Incumbent David Weprin advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after his only announced primary opponent, Mahtab Khan, was ruled off the ballot by the NYC Board of Elections for insufficient petition signatures. Welson Chang advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: David Weprin is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 24, first elected in 2010. He chairs the Assembly Insurance Committee and also serves on the Banks, Codes, Judiciary and Ways and Means committees. He previously served on the New York City Council from 2001 to 2010, chairing its Finance Committee.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in political science from the State University of New York at Albany and a J.D. from Hofstra University.
Appointed deputy superintendent of banks and secretary of the state banking board by Gov. Mario Cuomo; later worked in financial services.
Served on the New York City Council representing District 23 from 2001 to 2010, chairing the Council's Finance Committee for eight years.
Succeeded his brother, Mark Weprin, and father, former Assembly Speaker Saul Weprin, in representing the 24th Assembly District.

positions.summary: Sponsored a bill to delay the start of enforcement of the Manhattan central business district tolling program (congestion pricing) to no earlier than January 1, 2031, and issued a 2023 statement calling the program a "$1 Billion tax hike" on New Yorkers.
positions.quote: New Yorkers cannot afford this $1 Billion tax hike, which is being camouflaged...

record.text: Chairs the Assembly Insurance Committee (2023-2026); also serves on the Banks, Codes, Judiciary, and Ways and Means committees.
Previously chaired the Assembly Correction Committee (2019-2022) and the Task Force on People with Disabilities.

Sponsored A01747, which would delay the start date of central business district tolling (congestion pricing) enforcement to no earlier than January 1, 2031; referred to the Transportation Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.
Sponsored A00303, establishing a New York State commission to end mass incarceration and prevent violence; referred to the Correction Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.

Sponsored A01723 (with co-sponsors including Nily Rozic), restricting municipalities from using funds to build or expand immigration detention facilities without legislative approval and creating an oversight committee; referred to the Local Governments Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.
Voted yes on S10113, allowing a cannabis microbusiness licensee to conduct retail sales, which passed the Assembly 88-53 on June 5, 2026.
Voted yes on S3460, granting employees access to their personnel records, which passed the Assembly 92-49 on May 19, 2026.

candidates.name: Welson Chang

summary.text: Welson Chang is the Republican and Queens United Party nominee for NY State Assembly District 24, running against incumbent David Weprin. He is a member of the Queens Village Republican Club.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, or detailed news coverage of Chang's positions or background could be located and independently verified. He has not filed a campaign-finance summary with OpenSecrets as of this research date.
